  Two of my earlier calls were wrong. I dropped Voyager claiming "no solid institutional launch reel" — JPL has posted its own 1977 film, so that was just a bad search on my
  part. And I dropped Lennon as unembeddable, which was true of the clip I'd found but not of CBS's own archive upload. Both are in now.

  The embed gate earned its keep again: the Wellcome Library's IVF film blocks embedding (error 150), so that one is the Science Museum's instead — equally well sourced and
  it actually plays.

  The 17 I deliberately left

  Eight cannot be done — they predate film or were never filmed: Krakatoa (1883), Röntgen's X-rays, Einstein's 1905 papers, general relativity, Hubble's expanding universe,
  the discovery of fission, the Chicago Pile (built in secret, no cameras), and the first website.

  Nine I tried and failed to do to standard: Benz, the Eiffel Tower, the 1896 Olympics, Marconi, the Wright flight, the USSR's founding, penicillin, the 1931 China floods,
  and the double helix. Searching returned only "on this day" channels, AI-narrated recuts, or footage from the wrong decade — the Wright brothers' 1903 flight was
  photographed, not filmed; the best USSR hit was industrialisation footage from 1925–30; the Eiffel films are Edison's from 1900, eleven years late, and only on hobbyist
  channels. A card whose Wikipedia extract is accurate beats one that plays a video of something else. Say the word if you'd rather I take the best available on any of those
  nine and accept the weaker provenance.
